mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, as investors anticipate future rate hikes, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a given month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 2-year risk-free rate proxy by more than 0.5 percentage points in inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS labor compensation growth signals wage stickiness and labor market strength, which precedes a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month growth rate exceeds 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with high unemployment, 60-day forward returns do not exceed the average of the previous 12 months by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in GDPC1 personal consumption expenditure accompanied by a simultaneous rise in HOUST retail sales predicts a near-term demand expansion that drives positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 month-over-month increase > 2% AND HOUST month-over-month increase > 1%
failure_condition: During periods of high uncertainty, the 5-day forward return does not exceed the 5-day realized return by more than 0.2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO manufacturing index coinciding with a decline in RSAFS retail sales signals supply-side weakness, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month decline > 3% AND RSAFS month-over-month decline > 2%
failure_condition: In non-crisis regimes, the 20-day forward return remains non-negative despite sustained supply contraction for 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in FEDFUNDS below 1.5% for three consecutive months indicates a shift to accommodative policy, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns in non-recessionary regimes.
failure_condition: In recessionary regimes (as measured by UNRATE < 1%), 60-day forward returns do not exceed risk-free rates by more than 0.1 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE unemployment rate above 4.5% predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as market anticipates further job losses.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% in a given month
failure_condition: During periods of falling unemployment, the 20-day forward return does not fall below the 20-day realized return by more than 0.5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time positive surprise in GDPC1 personal consumption (vintage date) followed by two consecutive months of above-trend HOUST retail sales predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return due to transitory demand acceleration.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 vintage surprise > 0.5% AND HOUST next two months > previous trend
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes, the 5-day forward return does not beat the 5-day realized return by more than 0.3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO manufacturing index falls by more than 4% in a month and RSAFS retail sales decline by at least 3%, it indicates structural supply-side weakness that precedes a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly drop > 4% AND RSAFS monthly drop > 3%
failure_condition: In periods of excess capacity, the 20-day forward return remains non-negative despite sustained supply weakness for 60 days.
